tasks.short: Coordinate meetings, conferences and office events from initial brief through delivery.

steps.what: Agree the event purpose, audience, constraints and budget ceiling.
Request venue availability, catering options and prices.
Compare supplier quotes and prepare the event plan and cost estimate.

loop.input: Supplier quotes and the event brief.
loop.output: Source-linked prices, availability, capacity, exclusions and cancellation terms.
loop.check: Require source passages; validate currencies and totals; flag missing terms and conflicting dates.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per quote; unresolved fields go to the administrative assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier quotes use inconsistent prose and layouts. Calculations and comparison tables remain deterministic.

steps.what: Approve the event plan, supplier choice and spending limit.
Create invitations with the approved time, location and joining instructions.
Update attendance and practical requirements from invitation replies.
Confirm supplier bookings, final numbers and delivery instructions.
Coordinate arrivals, suppliers and unexpected changes during the event.

tasks.design: Configure an event record and response form in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to the {CALENDAR} and {EMAIL}. A bounded extraction loop reads supplier quotes; deterministic code calculates costs and generates plans and booking documents in the {DOCS}. People approve invitations and supplier commitments, while forms maintain attendance and surface exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event details arrive across conversations, quotes and replies. Existing calendar tools cover invitations but rarely connect supplier terms, spending approval and attendance requirements.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, calendar rules and reusable templates cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting them, while bounded extraction handles varied quotes.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier negotiation, accessibility arrangements and live changes require judgement. Cancellation terms and late headcount changes can alter the approved cost.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, negotiate trade-offs and recover calmly when arrangements fail.

ambition.what: Guided event booking for small departmental workshops.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer attendance updates and repeated supplier emails. Within an agreed budget and contingency allowance, the assistant can choose approved options and resolve routine changes.

reach.task: Compare venue capacity and supplier performance before renewing event arrangements.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, total event cost and supplier contract terms.

reach.task: Prepare room layouts and access arrangements for larger gatherings.
reach.learn: Occupancy limits, accessible routes and escalation procedures.

evidence.claim: Calendar rules, structured responses and templates can automate routine event administration; these time estimates are unvalidated planning assumptions.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can turn a mail thread into an invitation with an agenda; this supports invitation preparation, not complete event coordination.
The UK Department for Business and Trade evaluation found scheduling took longer on average, so model use alone does not establish a scheduling benefit.
GDPR requires proportionate handling of attendee data; national rules determine employee consultation obligations.

assumptions: The baseline represents a departmental event with outside suppliers, rather than a specialist conference operation.
Structured response forms replace most free-text attendance replies; unusual requirements remain exceptions.
Access to accessibility or dietary requirements is restricted, with a defined deletion period.
Routine supplier requests create no spending commitment. Bookings require approval and must match the approved scope.
Build ranges and remaining-time percentages are estimates, not results from the cited cases.
The access allowance includes a national consultation assessment; any required formal process may extend elapsed time.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. This design does not monitor staff or allocate their work.
unknowns: Typical event size, supplier count and frequency.
Existing form, calendar and approval capabilities.
Who may commit spending and approve changes.
Countries involved and applicable national consultation requirements.
Which attendee requirements are collected and how long they are retained.
research_questions: Can native calendar and form configuration cover attendance without custom integration?
How accurately can representative supplier quotes be extracted, including exclusions and cancellation terms?
new_work: Review extracted supplier terms and booking documents.
Resolve unusual attendance requirements and failed responses.
Maintain event templates, approval limits and supplier details.
Check permissions and delete attendee requirements on schedule.

tasks.short: Distribute approved newsletters, promotional material and routine information to the correct recipients.

steps.what: Check that supplied material, attachments and distribution instructions are complete.
Select recipients and export their contact details.
Remove duplicates, invalid addresses and recipients marked against promotional contact.
Assemble the mailing from approved text, images, links and recipient fields.
Approve the mailing preview, audience and planned release time.
Release the approved mailing and record delivery results.
Record failed deliveries, address corrections and unsubscribe requests.

tasks.design: Use live audience rules and suppression controls across the {CRM} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, removing the exported list and spreadsheet cleanup. Configure approved templates, previews and scheduled sending in the {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}; approval binds the content version and audience definition, with eligibility checked again at send time. Delivery failures and unsubscribes update contact records, while ambiguous replies enter a review queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audience exports separate contact permissions from the eventual send. Manual preparation persists where templates, suppression controls and approval records have not been configured together.
tasks.enabler_now: Most capabilities already exist in standard systems. Small integrations and configuration can connect them without a model or autonomous agent.
tasks.still_hard: Contact permissions can be incomplete or stale. A correct mailing process cannot resolve unclear audience ownership or unsuitable promotional content.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a message is useful and appropriate for its audience, and handle sensitive recipient replies.

ambition.what: Audience-specific distribution of approved operational updates.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time exporting addresses and assembling repeated mailings. They can schedule approved recurring updates within agreed audience rules; communications approval remains with the communications manager.

reach.task: Plan recurring office notices for employees, contractors and site contacts.
reach.learn: Audience definitions, communication calendars and delivery exception handling.

reach.task: Correct contact records from a reviewed delivery exception queue.
reach.learn: Contact matching, suppression precedence and traceable corrections.

evidence.claim: Audience rules, suppression lists, templates, approvals and scheduled sends are established deterministic capabilities.
Removing exported mailing lists can eliminate repeated manual cleanup when live audience and suppression controls replace it.
GDPR and applicable national electronic-marketing rules affect recipient selection, contact permissions and objection handling.

assumptions: Electronic distribution is the dominant case. Required postal batches need a separate print-and-dispatch branch.
Content is supplied and approved; writing a newsletter is outside this task.
Live suppression and duplicate controls replace spreadsheet cleanup rather than merely moving the export.
The send uses the recorded approval from the preceding step; it does not require a duplicate approval.
Audience or content changes invalidate approval. New suppressions always take precedence.
Build ranges and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates.
The access allowance includes assessing national consultation requirements; the design contains no employee monitoring.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; this design requires no model.
unknowns: The proportion of electronic and postal distribution.
Current audience sources and contact-permission records.
Whether existing systems support live audiences, approval binding and suppression synchronisation.
Who approves external communications and recurring operational notices.
Relevant countries and national electronic-marketing requirements.
research_questions: Can existing configuration remove audience exports entirely?
Do suppression changes reach every sending channel before a scheduled release?
Which recipient replies still require manual interpretation?
new_work: Maintain approved templates and audience definitions.
Review ambiguous replies and disputed address corrections.
Check suppression synchronisation and failed integrations.
Review recurring mailing approvals when content or audience rules change.

tasks.short: Create and maintain routine website and intranet pages using approved company information.

steps.what: Clarify the requested page change, audience, deadline and content owner.
Supply current facts, approved documents and usable images.
Draft page text and adapt supplied material for the intended audience.

loop.input: Page brief, approved source pack and page writing rules.
loop.output: Page text with source references and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Trace factual statements to supplied sources; preserve dates and figures; flag unsupported claims for review.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per page; unresolved claims return to the content owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied source prose needs condensation and audience-specific wording. Structured fields use direct templates instead.

steps.what: Enter text, images, links and metadata into a page template.
Check the page preview for layout, links, readability and accessibility problems.
Approve factual accuracy, audience access and publication.
Publish the approved page version.
Check the live page and record completion or defects.

tasks.design: Configure page templates, required fields, access settings and version approval in the {CMS}, with source packs held in the {DOCS}. A bounded model loop drafts prose only where supplied text needs adaptation; deterministic checks validate links, required fields and selected accessibility rules before human preview review. The {WORKFLOW} publishes the approved version, checks its live status and records defects in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Content arrives in inconsistent documents and emails, then requires repeated copying into page fields. Unclear ownership and approval delay updates even when the publishing tools already exist.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing page templates and publishing controls handle routine assembly. AI-assisted coding makes small connectors and checks cheaper, while a bounded drafting loop can adapt source prose.
tasks.still_hard: Someone must establish which source is current and whether information belongs on a public page. Automated checks cannot establish full accessibility, factual accuracy or visual quality.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the audience, resolve contradictory information and judge whether a page answers its practical question.

ambition.what: A scheduled freshness review for employee-facing procedure pages.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time copying text and chasing publication status. They can schedule routine updates to approved pages, while content owners retain factual and publication approval.

reach.task: Coordinate a procedure-page refresh across departments.
reach.learn: Dependency tracking, content ownership and acceptance criteria.

reach.task: Map approved source fields into reusable page templates.
reach.learn: Content schemas, access controls and integration failure handling.

evidence.claim: Page templates, version approval and scheduled publishing can handle routine website maintenance without autonomous agents.
Bounded drafting can adapt source prose, but factual and publication review remain necessary.
Deterministic checks can detect broken links and some accessibility defects; they do not establish complete accessibility.
The EU AI Act includes an AI literacy obligation relevant to staff using a drafting model.

assumptions: The typical task is routine content and template maintenance in an existing {CMS}. New application features need separate scope.
Existing {CMS} configuration supports structured templates, draft creation and versioned approval.
The content owner supplies authoritative sources and confirms image usage rights.
Publication approval is bound to the exact version and access setting. The publishing step consumes that approval.
External publication is used as the authority ceiling; intranet-only publication uses internal write authority.
The freshness review uses review dates and named owners, rather than inferred employee performance.
Build ranges and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. National rules determine whether employee consultation is required, and formal consultation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: The balance between public websites, intranet pages and custom development.
Existing {CMS} template, API, preview, permission and rollback capabilities.
Who owns each page and can approve public disclosure.
Current accessibility requirements and known template defects.
Applicable countries, national consultation requirements and approved model access.
research_questions: Can native {CMS} configuration populate drafts without custom code?
Which recurring page types can use direct field mapping instead of a model?
Which live-page failures can be detected reliably without a visual review?
new_work: Review generated prose against its sources.
Maintain source mappings, templates and page check rules.
Handle conflicting facts, missing approvals and publication failures.
Review page freshness reminders and verify accessibility beyond automated checks.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward handling exceptions, preparing decisions and keeping shared information useful. The assistant gains bounded scheduling and coordination discretion where delegated; spending, audience and publication approvals stay with their named owners.
reach: Administrative services management through event cost and supplier comparisons.
Project coordination through cross-department content refreshes.
Systems analysis through structured forms, source mappings and integration exceptions.
skills_to_grow: Translate recurring requests into forms, fields and approval rules.
Check source evidence and recognise unsupported generated text.
Manage supplier terms, budget limits and contingency decisions.
Apply contact permissions, data minimisation and access controls.
Diagnose failed workflows and maintain reusable templates.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a shared administrative service for small departmental events, targeted operational notices and current procedure pages, with clear service standards and delegated decision limits.

job.title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
